Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Keystone is progressing on the on-prem deployment and our security team has a few requests we need to close for our SOC2 readiness window: we need a concrete outbound (egress) allowlist for the Redwood private endpoint, the minimal set of ports/IPs/domains your control plane requires, and an evidence bundle showing a validation run (pcaps / traceroutes / signed statement) we can attach to our compliance binder.

Can you provide: 
- A canonical allowlist (IP / port / FQDN) for the private endpoint control plane and any optional telemetry endpoints. Please call out which entries are required for normal operation vs optional (batching/reporting).
- Any SNI/TLS inspection considerations (does traffic require passthrough? will mTLS be used to control plane?).
- Recommended firewall/NAT rules and outbound routing patterns (proxying through NGFW vs direct egress).
- A short acceptance test we can run to validate connectivity (commands and expected responses).

Also, our auditors want a short-lived break-glass mechanism for emergency connectivity during onboarding — they prefer a time-limited IP exception with logging. If you have standard wording and the evidence collection steps you use, please share.

We have a tentative deadline of 2027-06-10 to include artifacts in our binder. CC'ing Keystone Security.

Thanks,
Maya
Sr. Cloud Security Engineer
Keystone Health

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together the minimal set of steps and an evidence plan; attaching the allowlist matrix (keystone_egress_matrix.csv) and a short audit bundle template (audit_evidence_bundle.zip) for your team to use. High-level summary below — full details in the CSV.

1) Minimal egress table (required vs optional):
   - Required: TCP 443 to controlplane.redwood.ai (SNI: controlplane.redwood.ai) — TLS passthrough, mutual TLS optional but recommended for Private deployments.
   - Required: UDP 53 (DNS) to internal resolver(s) — if you use split-horizon DNS, ensure controlplane.redwood.ai resolves to the private endpoint IPs we provided.
   - Optional (telemetry/metrics): TCP 443 to metrics.redwood.ai and logs.redwood.ai — can be routed via an internal proxy to avoid direct internet egress.
   - Backchannel (ops debug): TCP 22022 to maintenance-ssh.redwood.ai (restricted by client certs) — only for scheduled maintenance.

2) Firewall / NAT guidance (patterns we recommend):
   - Pin outbound flows to customer-owned NAT IPs for auditability. Redwood expects consistent source IPs for allowlisting; ephemeral dynamic source IPs will complicate tracing.
   - Where possible, route all Redwood control-plane egress via an internal forward proxy (corporate NGFW) that logs TLS SNI and destination IPs. For full end-to-end integrity, prefer connection pass-through with TLS untouched; rely on mTLS at application layer if you require payload-level assurance.

3) SNI & TLS inspection notes:
   - Control-plane sessions are standard TLS. Redwood supports mTLS if you configure client certs during onboarding — we recommend mTLS for regulated workloads. If your proxy performs TLS termination/inspection, ensure it preserves or logs original SNI (controlplane.redwood.ai) and that re-minted certs include the same SANs; otherwise use a passthrough rule for controlplane traffic.

4) Break-glass (time-limited exception) pattern:
   - Issue: temporary IP 198.51.100.45 as a 48-hour exception.
   - Controls: ticketed approval (security owner + product), automated logging to SIEM, and mandatory packet-capture submission to Redwood engineers after the window.

5) Acceptance test (runnable):
   - DNS: dig +short controlplane.redwood.ai @<your-resolver> (expect private endpoint IPs provided in the onboarding doc)
   - TLS: openssl s_client -connect <endpoint-ip>:443 -servername controlplane.redwood.ai (expect certificate with CN/SAN controlplane.redwood.ai)
   - mTLS check: curl --cert client.crt --key client.key https://controlplane.redwood.ai/healthz (200 OK)

6) Evidence bundle we provide: 
   - Signed statement from Redwood (included in audit_evidence_bundle.zip)
   - Sample traceroute and tcpdump output for the acceptance test (templates in ZIP)
   - Allowlist CSV (keystone_egress_matrix.csv) with required/optional flags, ports, and rationales.

Next actions: Laura — can you confirm we'll include the signed statement in the ZIP and finalize the proposed break-glass IP? Olga — can you create the traceroute/tcpdump outputs against Keystone's private endpoint once they are live? Maya — if you send the resolver IPs and the private endpoint IPs you want us to validate against, we'll run the tests and return the filled evidence bundle by EOD Monday (2027-06-07).

Best,
Markus Klein

Thanks Markus — filing this into Keystone's compliance tracker. Maya: quick clarifications from acceptance criteria side so audits can sign off cleanly:

- Evidence must include timestamps (UTC) and MD5 hashes for any pcap/traceroute files; the audit bundle template has the expected filename format (keystone-<YYYYMMDD>-<test>-pcap).
- For the break-glass IP we prefer: 198.51.100.45 for 48 hours and a secondary fallback 198.51.100.46 for an additional 24 hours if extended approval is given. Both should be logged with a ticket reference (Keystone-TKT-####).
- If you choose proxy inspection, include the proxy certificate chain in the bundle and a short note describing whether SNI is preserved. If SNI is not preserved, we will require passthrough for the control-plane hostnames.

I'll take responsibility for the signed statement and will sign it once Markus' team confirms the final CSV entries. Expect the signed statement and the completed ZIP back from us by 2027-06-07 EOD assuming your resolver IPs are received.

Laura Bennett
